is_required.description: Whether this parameter must be supplied before the step runs.

value_type.description: Expected value type for this parameter.

format.description: Optional string subtype hint; only applies when value_type is string.

default_value.description: Author-supplied default; pre-fills the run panel and is used when no caller value is supplied.

options.description: radio/checkbox: the choices the runner picks from.

min_choices.description: checkbox: minimum number of choices that must be selected.

max_choices.description: checkbox: maximum number of choices that may be selected.

property_path.description: JSON path into the webhook response (e.g. $.data.id or items[0].name).

parameter.description: Parameter name to bind to the value at property_path.

default_value.description: Fallback value for the parameter when the response omits property_path.

id.description: Unique identifier for the next step.

condition_parameter.description: Name of a parameter (resolved from an earlier step's response) that gates this transition. An empty string means the transition is unconditional. When condition_expected is omitted, the transition runs only when this parameter resolves to a truthy value. An unresolved parameter is treated as false. A query step's scalar RETURN columns are bound automatically under their alias, so a boolean projection ("... AS hasExistingConnection") can gate a branch without an explicit response_parameters mapping; a name already resolved is left alone, so an explicit mapping is still required to overwrite one.

condition_expected.description: Optional expected boolean result for condition_parameter. When present, the transition runs only when the parameter's strict boolean value ("true"/"1" -> true; "false"/"0"/anything else/unresolved -> false) equals this value. Lets two sibling transitions branch on a single parameter — one expecting true, the other false.

query_id.description: Query id this step executes. Empty string when the step runs a custom endpoint or Local LLM config instead.

kind.description: Set to "local_llm" when the step runs a saved Ollama config instead of a query or HTTP endpoint. Omitted for query/endpoint steps.

config_id.description: Catalog local_llm_configs row id. Only present when kind is "local_llm".

endpoint.description: Webhook endpoint URL. Empty string when the step runs a query instead.

method.description: HTTP method used when calling the endpoint.

headers.description: HTTP headers sent to the endpoint.

body.description: JSON body sent to the endpoint.

parameters.description: Parameter definitions for values referenced by this step (request body / inputs).

next.description: Outgoing transitions from this step, in evaluation order.

availableParameters.description: The names one step publishes into run state. Compose-time introspection: it is what a loop condition or for-each source may reference, and what the builder offers in its picker.

step_id.description: The step that publishes these names.

aliases.description: Identifier-shaped names this step binds: an operation-backed step's RETURN aliases, or the parameters an endpoint/LLM step's response_parameters mappings write.

loopCondition.description: A for/while test, evaluated against run state before each pass.

parameter.description: Name to test — a sequence/step parameter, or a RETURN alias a step publishes.

operator.description: Comparison to apply. Mirrors QUERY-package.schema.json returnItem.comparison_operator so a loop test offers the same vocabulary as a boolean RETURN projection.

value.description: Right-hand side. Typed by the operands at run time: a boolean on the left compares as a boolean, two numeric-looking operands compare numerically, anything else compares as text. An unresolved parameter reads as the empty string, so a missing value ends the loop rather than spinning.

loop.description: How this run's one cycle terminates. Absent for a plain DAG walk, where a transition back to an earlier step simply ends (a step runs at most once). Present only when the sequence selected a loop type AND its steps contain exactly one cycle.

type.description: The termination rule. "dag" never appears here — it produces no descriptor at all.

max_iterations.description: Hard cap on passes through the body. Exceeding it aborts the run with status "error" rather than spinning against the graph.

back_edge.description: The transition that closes the cycle, found structurally rather than authored. While iterating, the executor follows only this edge; once the loop ends, only the source step's other outgoing edges.

from.description: The step the back-edge leaves — the cycle's tail, where the termination rule is evaluated.

to.description: The step the back-edge returns to — the cycle's entry, where the pre-test runs before the first pass.

body.description: Every step enclosed by the cycle: reachable from the entry and able to reach the tail. These leave the visited set at each iteration boundary so they run again; steps outside stay visited, which is what keeps a fan-in before or after the loop running exactly once.

count.description: for: how many passes to make. Zero skips the body entirely.

condition.description: for_while: the pre-test. Checked before the first pass too, so a condition that is already false skips the body.

source.description: for_each: the RETURN alias whose result set is iterated, one pass per row.

source_step.description: for_each: the step that projects source, resolved at compose time. Named explicitly because an empty result set has no row to recognize the alias in — without it the executor could not tell "the source returned nothing" (skip the body) from "this step is not the source".

steps.description: Ordered list of steps in this execution sequence.

response_parameters.description: Sequence-level response mappings shared across steps. When a step runs, values at each property_path are bound to the named parameter for downstream steps; default_value applies when the path is missing.

available_parameters.description: Per-step catalogue of the names the sequence's steps publish into run state. Consumed by the builder's loop pickers and by compose-time validation of a loop config; the executor does not read it.
